title: Word Concatenation Substrings
statement:
Find every place where a string contains all required words back-to-back in any order.

Contract
- `text` and `words` are non-null. Every word is non-null, non-empty, and all words have the same length.
- Return the starting indices, in increasing order, where the substring of length `words.length * wordLength` can be split into words that match `words` with exactly the same multiplicities.
- The words may appear in any order inside the window. Overlapping answers are allowed.
- If `words` is empty, or the combined length is longer than `text`, return an empty list.

Examples
- In `barfoothefoobarman` with `[foo, bar]`, return `[0, 9]`.
- In `wordgoodgoodgoodbestword` with `[word, good, best, good]`, return `[8]`.
- In `aaaaaa` with `[aa, aa]`, return `[0, 1, 2]`.

examples.input: text = wordgoodgoodgoodbestword, words = [word, good, best, good]

hints: All words have the same length, so valid starts fall into word-length offsets.
For each offset, slide a window by whole words and keep counts of words currently inside it.
When a word appears too many times, advance the left edge until the count is legal again. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(m) space for the word counts.
inputSyntax: Input: text followed by a bracketed word list, for example: barfoothefoobarman [foo, bar]
